Last updated November 14, 2026.

Fort Collins at a glance

Selling in Fort Collins?
We buy Fort Collins houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

What kind of city is Fort Collins for a home seller?

Fort Collins is a home rule city and the county seat of Larimer County, built along the Cache la Poudre River at the foot of the Front Range foothills, about 60 miles north of Denver. It is the fourth-largest city in Colorado, with 169,810 residents at the 2020 census and a 2024 estimate of 170,924.

A city this size has several kinds of housing, from older homes near the historic Old Town district to neighborhoods that spread south as the city grew in the late twentieth century. Sellers here range from long-time owners to landlords and heirs, and the right way to sell depends mostly on the condition of the house and how quickly you need to move.

How did Fort Collins begin?

Fort Collins began as a U.S. Army post. The fort was established in 1864 as the successor to Camp Collins, which a June 1864 flood destroyed, and the Army decommissioned it in 1867.

The town was platted in 1867, and the county seat moved from LaPorte to Fort Collins in 1868. Colorado Agricultural College was founded in 1870 and held its first classes in 1879.

Wikipedia gives two different incorporation dates, so we leave the year out here. The article also notes that the Northern Arapaho were centered on the Cache la Poudre Valley before the city existed.

Fort Collins at a glance

These figures are taken from the Wikipedia article on the city.

ItemFigure
2020 census population169,810
2024 estimate170,924
Total area58.473 square miles
Elevationabout 5,000 feet (sources give 4,982 to 4,997)
Average annual precipitation15.88 inches
Average annual snowfall51.4 inches
Coldest monthDecember, 31.1 degrees F average
Form of governmentCouncil-manager, seven-member council

Who are the biggest employers in Fort Collins?

Colorado State University is the largest employer in Fort Collins, with 8,850 employees in the city's 2024 annual financial report. That anchor of public jobs keeps demand for housing steady near campus and in the neighborhoods around it.

EmployerEmployees (2024)
Colorado State University8,850
University of Colorado Hospital Authority5,900
Poudre School District R-14,600
City of Fort Collins2,550
Larimer County2,550
Woodward, Inc.1,350
Broadcom Inc.1,050

The city also lists manufacturing, clean energy, bioscience and agri-tech in its economy, and nearly 200,000 people were employed as of July 2025. A job change for you or a new buyer often drives the timing of a sale.

Which school district covers Fort Collins?

Poudre School District runs the public K-12 schools in Fort Collins and nearby towns. It operates four comprehensive high schools, four alternative high schools, ten middle schools and 32 elementary schools, and it adds about 400 to 500 students each year.

Charter and private options exist as well. A buyer's school questions usually come down to the attendance zone for a single address, so have that answer ready or tell the buyer to ask the district.

How do people get around Fort Collins?

Interstate 25 runs north to south along the east side of the city, and US 287 becomes College Avenue, the busiest street in town.

  • MAX Bus Rapid Transit follows the Mason Corridor parallel to College Avenue, from downtown to a transit center south of Harmony Road. It opened in May 2014 and takes about 15 minutes end to end.
  • Transfort is the city bus system, with more than a dozen routes.
  • Northern Colorado Regional Airport is nearby, and Denver International Airport is about 70 miles south.

Homes near MAX stops and College Avenue draw a different set of buyers and renters than houses in the outer neighborhoods, and that is worth mentioning when you describe your property.

What happened in the 1997 Fort Collins flood?

In July 1997 a flash flood followed about 31 hours of rain totaling 10 to 14 inches. It killed five people, caused about $5 million in damage to city property and roughly $140 million in damage to Colorado State University, including flooding its library.

After an event like that, flood status is a fair question to expect. If your house lies near the Poudre or one of its drainage channels, a buyer or lender will want to know its flood zone status. A cash buyer will look at the same facts but will not need a lender's flood determination to close.

Does Fort Collins require landlords to register rentals?

Yes. Since January 1, 2025, most long-term rental properties, meaning homes rented for 30 days or more, must register annually with the city and certify that they meet minimum housing standards.

If you own a rental and plan to sell, this affects you in a few ways:

  • A buyer who intends to keep the tenants will ask whether the registration is current.
  • The city runs a Rental Housing program with grants for landlord repairs and says funding rounds typically open in December for the following year.
  • The program's office is at 281 N College Ave and can be reached at 970-416-2305 or rentalhousing@fortcollins.gov.

Selling a rented house with tenants in place is possible. A direct sale to an investor often works for owners who do not want to vacate a unit or fix deferred items first.

When are Larimer County property taxes due?

For 2025 taxes payable in 2026, Larimer County set February 28 for the first half, June 15 for the second half, and April 30 for payment in full. February 28 fell on a Saturday that year, and payments received the following Monday, March 2, were treated as timely.

Payments can be made online by credit or debit card or by electronic check, which has no fee. You can also mail a check to the Larimer County Treasurer, P.O. Box 2336, Fort Collins, CO 80522, or pay in person at 200 W. Oak St., Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. The treasurer's phone is (970) 498-7020.

Late payments carry interest under Colorado law. If a mortgage escrow pays your taxes, ask your servicer for the payoff and escrow refund details. The county page does not describe proration at closing, so your title company is the right source for how the tax is split.

What does it cost to record a deed in Colorado?

Colorado's documentary fee is one cent per $100 of consideration on a deed conveying real property, and any partial $100 counts as a full one. It is paid to the county clerk and recorder, and no fee applies if the consideration is $500 or less.

On a $400,000 sale, the fee comes to $400. Your purchase contract states which party pays it.

How does a direct cash sale of a Fort Collins house work?

A direct sale replaces the listing process with a short list of steps, and you can stop at any of them.

  • You describe the house, its condition and the date you would like to close.
  • The buyer reviews the details and may walk through the property.
  • You get an offer and decide whether to accept it.
  • A title company checks ownership, orders the tax certificate and prepares the closing papers.
  • You sign the deed, it is recorded with the Larimer County clerk and recorder, and you receive the proceeds.

Since the buyer pays with cash, no lender appraisal or loan approval sits in the middle of the timeline. We cannot quote a price or a closing date without seeing the property, and we do not promise either in advance.

More questions about Fort Collins, CO

Can I sell a Fort Collins rental with tenants in it?

Yes. You can sell a rental that is still occupied, and an investor buyer may keep the tenants. If the property was registered with the city under the 2025 rental program, make sure the registration is current before closing.

Do I need to repair my Fort Collins house before selling?

No. A cash sale is made as-is, so the buyer prices the repairs into the offer. You skip contractor bids, inspections ordered by a lender and showings.

When is the Larimer County property tax deadline?

For taxes payable in 2026, the first half was due February 28, the full payment option was due April 30, and the second half is due June 15. The county treasurer can confirm dates for the current year.

Is Fort Collins in a flood area?

Parts of it are near the Cache la Poudre River and drainage channels. A 1997 flash flood killed five people and caused heavy damage, so buyers often check a parcel's flood zone. Look up your address on the city's maps.

What is the Colorado deed fee on a home sale?

One cent per $100 of the price, paid to the county clerk and recorder when the deed is recorded. The sales contract decides who pays it.

Grand Junction at a glance

Selling in Grand Junction?

Where is Grand Junction, and how big is it?

Grand Junction is a home rule city and the county seat of Mesa County, 247 miles west-southwest of Denver, and the largest city in Colorado outside the Front Range Urban Corridor. It is the economic and cultural center of the Western Slope.

The 2020 census counted 65,560 residents, which made it the 17th most populous municipality in the state, and the 2025 estimate shown on Wikipedia is 71,780. The city covers about 40 square miles at an elevation of 4,646 feet.

Grand Junction facts in one table

ItemFigure
IncorporatedJuly 22, 1882
2020 census population65,560
2025 estimate (Wikipedia infobox)71,780
Total area40.077 square miles
Elevation4,646 feet
Average annual precipitationabout 9 inches
Average annual snowfall17.6 inches
Sunshinejust over 3,200 hours a year

The source article also gives a metro population of over 162,000 for 2025, which is a wider area than the city itself.

How did Grand Junction get its name and start?

The name refers to the junction of the Colorado River, once called the Grand River, with the Gunnison River. Before incorporation, the community was known as Ute.

The Ute people lived in the region before European-American farmers arrived in the 1880s. In September 1881 the former Ute Indian Territory was abolished and the Utes were moved to a reservation. George Addison Crawford incorporated the town on July 22, 1882. Railroads reached the city in 1882 from Pueblo by narrow gauge and in 1890 by standard gauge from New Castle.

Fruit growing became important by the late nineteenth century, especially between Grand Junction and Palisade, with peaches, pears, apricots, plums, cherries and grapes. Wineries opened in the area beginning in the late twentieth century.

What does the high desert climate mean for a house?

Grand Junction has a cold semi-arid climate with hot summers and about 9 inches of precipitation a year, so roofs and exteriors face sun and heat more than rain.

  • July averages 78.2 degrees F, and January averages 27.4 degrees F.
  • About 68 days a year reach 90 degrees or higher, and about 8 days reach 100 degrees or higher.
  • The average last freeze is April 25 and the average first freeze is October 11.

Long stretches of heat are hard on air conditioners, roofing and exterior paint. A buyer's inspector will often check the cooling system and the roof, and a cash buyer prices what they find instead of asking you to repair it.

What drives Grand Junction's economy?

Health care, tourism, agriculture, livestock and energy are the main contributors, according to Wikipedia. The largest employers it lists give a sense of the job base.

EmployerEmployees
Mesa County Valley School District 513,465
St. Mary's Regional Hospital2,846
Colorado Mesa University1,173

Energy has a history of boom and bust here. Oil shale development lifted the area in the 1970s and early 1980s, and Exxon's withdrawal in 1982, known locally as Black Sunday, caused an economic bust.

Which schools and college are in Grand Junction?

Mesa County Valley School District 51 provides public K-12 education in the area. Wikipedia names Fruita Monument, Grand Junction, Central and Palisade high schools among its five, plus an R-5 High School.

Colorado Mesa University enrolls nearly 10,000 students and is the largest university in western Colorado. Owners of rentals near campus are one group that sometimes decides to sell.

What roads, rail and flights serve Grand Junction?

Interstate 70 links Grand Junction east to Glenwood Springs and Denver and west toward Green River, Utah. U.S. Highways 6 and 50 also meet in the city, and State Highway 340 runs through the Redlands to Fruita.

  • Grand Junction Regional Airport is the largest airport in western Colorado and the third largest in the state.
  • Amtrak's California Zephyr stops at Grand Junction Station.
  • Grand Valley Transit provides local buses, and Bustang offers intercity service.

The city sits in the Grand Valley, a river valley about 30 miles long. Nearby areas include the Redlands, Palisade, Fruita and Loma, and a buyer may compare a house in the city with homes in those communities.

Are short-term rentals regulated in Grand Junction?

Yes. Any property owner who plans to run a short-term rental inside city limits must get a license from the City of Grand Junction and renew it every year, under Ordinance No. 5163 adopted July 5, 2023.

The application fee is $275 per property. The city also caps how many residentially zoned lots can hold a primary short-term rental.

  • Downtown (North Ave to I-70B, Highway 50 to N 17th St): no more than 7 percent of residentially zoned lots.
  • Outside downtown: no more than 3 percent.
  • Lots with four or fewer units: one primary and one secondary rental allowed.
  • Lots with five or more units: no more than 10 percent of units.

If you own a house that has been run as a short-term rental, check whether the license is current before talking to a buyer, because the cap affects who can get a new license. Community Development is at 250 N 5th Street and can be reached at 970-244-1430. The city page does not say whether a license transfers on sale, so ask the office.

When are Mesa County property taxes due?

Mesa County's assessor lists the key dates: the Treasurer mails tax bills on January 31, the first installment is due February 28, full payment is due April 30 and the second installment is due June 15.

DateEvent
January 1Property is valued as of this date
January 31Treasurer mails tax bills
February 28First installment due
April 30Full-year payment due
May 1Real property valuation notices mailed
June 8Last day to file a real property protest
June 15Second installment due

If you sell between January and the payment dates, the tax for the prior year may still be unpaid, so the title company will want to see the balance.

What does the state charge to record a deed?

Colorado's documentary fee is one cent per $100 of consideration on a deed conveying real property, with any partial $100 counted as a full one. It is paid to the county clerk and recorder, and nothing is owed at $500 or less.

On a $300,000 sale that comes to $300. The contract usually names the party who pays it.

How does a cash sale work in Grand Junction?

You contact us with the address and condition, we review it, and you get an offer you can accept or decline. A title company confirms ownership, orders the tax certificate and prepares the deed, and the deed is recorded in Mesa County.

There is no lender in the middle, so closing depends on title work and the date you choose. We do not promise a price or a timeline before we see the house.

More questions about Grand Junction, CO

What county is Grand Junction in?

Mesa County. Grand Junction is the county seat and the largest city in the county, so property taxes are billed by the Mesa County Treasurer and deeds are recorded in Mesa County.

When is the second property tax payment due in Mesa County?

June 15. The first installment is due February 28, and paying in full is due April 30, according to the Mesa County assessor's key dates page.

Do I need a license to rent my Grand Junction house short term?

Yes. The city requires an annual short-term rental license with a $275 application fee per property, and it limits the share of residential lots that can have a primary short-term rental.

Can I sell my Grand Junction house without repairs?

Yes. A cash buyer purchases as-is, so you do not have to fix the roof, cooling system or cosmetic items first. The offer reflects the condition.

How hot does Grand Junction get?

About 68 days a year reach 90 degrees F or higher, and about 8 days reach 100 or higher. That heat is why inspectors look closely at cooling systems and roofs.

Erie at a glance

Selling in Erie?

Get My Cash Offer →

Where is Erie, Colorado, and why does the county line matter to a seller?

Erie is a home rule town in the southwest corner of Weld County and the east edge of Boulder County, with about 58 percent of residents on the Weld side and 42 percent on the Boulder side. That split decides which county treasurer bills your property tax and which county clerk records your deed.

The town sits roughly 25 minutes from Denver and 20 minutes from Boulder, and about 35 minutes from Denver International Airport. Broomfield borders it to the south and Lafayette to the southwest. Erie uses the ZIP codes 80514 and 80516.

If you are selling, check your tax bill or the county parcel search first. Whether the house is in Weld or Boulder County tells you who to call for a tax payoff figure and where the sale paperwork will be filed.

What are the basic facts about Erie?

The figures below come from the Wikipedia article on the town and give a quick picture of who lives here and how big the place is.

ItemFigure
Settled1867
IncorporatedNovember 16, 1874
2020 census population30,038 (up 65.6 percent from 2010)
2024 population estimate38,594
Households10,047
Median household income$99,804
Median age37.4
Town area19.838 square miles
Planning area48 square miles
Elevationabout 5,072 feet

Erie is the most populous statutory town in Colorado, which is a legal category and not a measure of how it feels on the ground. Most of that growth happened in the last two decades.

How did Erie start, and does the coal history still affect houses?

Erie began as a coal town. Coal turned up in the mid-1860s in the southwest corner of Weld County, and the town took its name from Erie, Pennsylvania, the old home of early settler Richard Van Valkenburg.

Railroads arrived in 1870 and 1871 and carried coal toward Denver and nearby communities. The first official underground mine opened in 1876 under Ira Austin. Unlike a temporary mining camp, miners here owned homes in town.

Most local mines had closed by 1960, and the Eagle Mine shut in 1978. For a seller, the practical point is that older homes near the original town center may carry old additions, older plumbing and electrical systems, and records that take more digging to assemble. A buyer who purchases as-is does not need all of that fixed before closing.

Floods are also part of the record. Major floods hit in 1890, 1921 and 1972, and a dike was built around Coal Creek after the 1972 flood. If your lot is near the creek, expect a buyer or lender to ask about flood zone status.

How fast has Erie grown, and what does that mean for sellers?

Erie grew 65.6 percent between the 2010 and 2020 censuses, from roughly 18,100 residents to 30,038, and the 2024 estimate is 38,594. That pace suggests that a large share of local homes are fairly new compared with other Colorado towns.

For a seller, newer construction can mean fewer deferred repairs but also more neighbors offering similar homes. Some common situations we hear about in fast-growing suburbs include:

  • Homeowners who need to relocate for work before a listing could reasonably wrap up.
  • Owners of an inherited house who live out of state.
  • Landlords tired of managing a rental from a distance.
  • Sellers carrying a mortgage on a house that needs a new roof, flooring or paint.

None of these need a retail listing to be solved. A direct sale to a cash buyer skips showings, staging and buyer financing contingencies, which is the main reason people in these situations ask about it.

What roads, transit and airports serve Erie?

Interstate 25 runs along Erie's eastern border at Exit 232, and from there it is about 22 miles south to downtown Denver and 41 miles north to Fort Collins.

  • E-470 lies to the south.
  • State Highway 7 and State Highway 52 cross the area.
  • US 287 forms the western boundary.
  • Erie Municipal Airport (EIK) is town-owned, about three miles west of I-25 on Highway 7, with a 4,700-foot concrete runway.

Access to I-25 and E-470 is one reason commuters buy here, and it is a point worth stating in any sale conversation. Buyers who drive to Denver, Boulder or the north Front Range tend to ask about commute times first.

Which schools serve Erie homes?

Erie High School is the only high school in the town and belongs to the St. Vrain Valley School District. It opened in 2005 and was expanded in 2018, and it enrolled 1,727 students in the 2024-2025 school year.

Wikipedia notes that the school has paused open enrollment because of overcapacity, so students outside its attendance zone are not admitted. That makes the school zone worth confirming before any buyer assumes access. Parents often ask which school a specific address feeds, and the district can answer by address.

We have not confirmed the district boundaries for every Erie neighborhood, so check with the district if a zone matters to your sale.

What is Erie's weather, and how does it affect a house?

Erie has a dry Front Range climate with average annual precipitation of 16.17 inches. May is the wettest month at 2.60 inches and January is the driest at 0.57 inches.

Dry air does not mean low risk to the structure. Roofs, gutters, decks and exterior paint take sun and wind year-round, and an older roof is one of the first items a buyer's inspector flags. A cash buyer prices a worn roof into the offer and does not ask you to replace it first.

When are property taxes due in Weld County, and what happens at closing?

On the Weld County side, taxes are due January 1 for the previous year and can be paid in full by April 30 or in two halves, the first by February 28 and the second by June 15. Weld's treasurer states that partial payments are not accepted and that postmarks on or before the due date count.

OptionDue date (2026)
First halfFebruary 28
Second halfJune 15
Full paymentApril 30

Late interest rises by month. For example, the first half picks up 1 percent in March and 6 percent by August. Weld offers payment online at weldtax.com, by mail to PO Box 458, Greeley, or in person at 1400 N 17th Avenue, Greeley.

If your parcel is on the Boulder County side, the Boulder County Treasurer collects the tax, so confirm the figures with that office. The title company usually orders a certificate of taxes due and handles the proration at closing. Weld lists a Certificate of Taxes Due request form on its treasurer pages.

What does Colorado charge to record a deed?

Colorado charges a documentary fee of one cent per $100 of consideration on a deed recorded for real property, with any partial $100 counted as a full one. The fee is paid to the county clerk and recorder, and the statute sets no fee at or below $500.

On a $500,000 sale, one cent per $100 works out to $500. Who pays it is usually settled in the purchase contract, so read that line before you sign.

How does a cash sale of an Erie house work?

A cash sale follows a short sequence of steps, and you decide at each stage whether to go on.

  • You share the address, condition and your timing.
  • The buyer reviews the property and may visit it.
  • You receive an offer, and you can accept, counter or decline.
  • A title company runs the title search, orders tax figures and prepares the deed.
  • You sign, the deed is recorded with the county clerk where the parcel sits, and you are paid.

Because no lender is involved, there is no appraisal or loan approval to wait on. The pace is set mostly by title work and your preferred closing date. We do not promise a price or a timeline before we see the house.

More questions about Erie, CO

Which county is Erie, Colorado in?

Both. Erie lies mostly in southwest Weld County (about 58 percent of residents) and partly in eastern Boulder County (about 42 percent). Your tax bill shows which county covers your parcel.

Can I sell my Erie house as-is?

Yes. Homeowners can sell in current condition to a cash buyer without repairs, cleaning or staging. The offer reflects what the house needs, so a worn roof or dated kitchen lowers the number but does not block the sale.

Who pays property tax when an Erie house sells?

The title company usually prorates it between seller and buyer at closing based on a certificate of taxes due. Colorado bills taxes in arrears, so the seller typically owes a share for the months owned. Ask your title officer for the exact split.

How much is the state deed fee in Colorado?

The documentary fee is one cent per $100 of the sale price, paid to the county clerk and recorder when a deed is recorded. The contract decides which side pays it.

Does being near Coal Creek affect my sale?

It can. Erie had major floods in 1890, 1921 and 1972, and a dike was built along Coal Creek afterward. Buyers and lenders may check flood zone status for homes near the creek, so find out your parcel's status before you list or sell.

Fountain at a glance

Selling in Fountain?

Get My Cash Offer →

Where is Fountain, Colorado?

Fountain is a home rule city in El Paso County, about 10 miles south of downtown Colorado Springs and just east of Fort Carson. It belongs to the Colorado Springs metropolitan area and the Front Range Urban Corridor.

The city was named for Fountain Creek, which flows south through town. Fort Carson is the neighboring installation, and many sellers here have some tie to it. We found no sourced employment figure for the base, so we leave numbers out.

Fountain by the numbers

The table summarizes figures from the Wikipedia article on Fountain, which reports 2020 census data and a later estimate.

ItemFigure
2020 census population29,802 (up 15.3 percent from 25,846 in 2010)
2024 estimate29,457
Households9,931
Housing units10,324 (3.8 percent vacant)
Median age30.4
Total area22.367 square miles
Elevation5,558 feet

A 3.8 percent vacancy rate at the 2020 census means most of the housing stock was occupied, so a vacant house stands out to buyers and to neighbors.

What is the history of Fountain?

Fountain was founded in 1859 as a railroad shipping center for ranches and farms in the area. Wikipedia lists April 23, 1903 as the incorporation date in its infobox but says 1900 in the text, so we do not give a firm year.

One event from the early years still gets retold. On May 14, 1888, a freight train carrying about 18 tons of explosives collided with a passenger train in the city. Three people died, and the blast left a crater roughly 40 feet wide and 15 feet deep.

More recently, The New York Times called Fountain "America's Millennium City" in 1999, and the city won an All-America City award in 2002.

Which school districts serve Fountain?

Most of Fountain lies inside Fountain School District 8. The northern part of the city sits in Widefield School District 3, and small southern and northern slivers fall into Hanover School District 28 and Harrison School District 2.

  • Fountain School District 8 covers most addresses.
  • Widefield School District 3 covers the north end.
  • Hanover District 28 and Harrison District 2 touch small portions.

Buyers often ask which district a given address belongs to. Check the county parcel data or ask the district before you answer.

How are water and electric service handled in Fountain?

The city runs its own utility. City of Fountain Utilities was established in 1919 and provides water and electric service to roughly 48,000 people in and around Fountain.

Its office is at 101 N Main St, and the phone number is (719) 322-2010. When a house sells, the seller schedules a final reading and the buyer opens a new account, so call the utility early, especially if you have a past-due balance.

Wikipedia also records a long-running PFAS contamination problem linked to a nearby Air Force base, and notes that the city said in 2020 that its water was safe to drink. Because the topic worries some buyers, have the city's water quality information on hand if it comes up.

How do you get around Fountain?

Fountain is served by a municipal bus that links the city to Pikes Peak State College, and by Bustang's Outrider line connecting Lamar, Pueblo and Colorado Springs.

We did not confirm highway details from an official page, so we leave them out.

What should a Fountain seller line up before closing?

A short checklist keeps a Fountain sale from stalling over small items.

  • Find your property tax status with the El Paso County Treasurer and ask for a payoff figure if anything is unpaid.
  • Call City of Fountain Utilities at (719) 322-2010 about a final meter reading for water and electric service.
  • Confirm your school district by address, since four districts touch the city.
  • Gather any prior-owner paperwork, permits and repair receipts you have.
  • Decide who will pay the Colorado deed fee, and write that into the contract.

The utility's own page also lists tools for customers, including an outage map, bill assistance, utility easement information and a note about calling 811 before digging. If your yard has an easement, tell the buyer, because it can limit fences and additions.

Fountain's population was nearly flat in recent years: 29,802 at the 2020 census and an estimate of 29,457 for 2024, a decline of about 1.2 percent. A flat population means a house here competes for the same pool of buyers each year, and condition counts for a lot when you compare listings.

What is the city's water-rights story, and why does it matter?

In 2008 Fountain bought the 480-acre H2O Ranch in Custer County for $3.5 million, mainly for its water rights.

Water supply is a common question for Colorado buyers. The purchase gives you a documented answer if someone asks where the city's water comes from, though we cannot tie it to any change in house prices.

How are El Paso County property taxes paid?

El Paso County lets owners pay online through the treasurer's portal, by mail to P.O. Box 2018, Colorado Springs, CO 80901-2018, or in person at the Citizens Service Center, 1675 West Garden of the Gods Road, Suite 2100, Monday to Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. The county also offers monthly prepayment installments through EquaPay.

For a sale, the treasurer issues a Certificate of Taxes Due to verify the tax status of a property. Unpaid prior-year balances can be sold at the county's tax lien sale, so check for liens before closing. You can call (719) 520-7900 for a payoff figure.

The treasurer's main page links to an Important Dates page for the current deadlines, and we did not confirm those dates, so check it directly. Colorado's standard pattern, shown on Mesa County's assessor page, is full payment by April 30 or two halves due the end of February and June 15.

What does it cost to record a deed in Colorado?

Colorado's documentary fee is one cent per $100 of consideration on a deed to real property, rounding any partial $100 up. It is paid to the county clerk and recorder, and consideration of $500 or less owes nothing.

For a $350,000 sale the fee is $350. The purchase contract says who pays.

What is a cash sale like in Fountain?

A cash sale keeps the steps short. You tell us about the house, we review it, and you receive an offer you can accept or turn down. A title company then verifies ownership, orders the tax certificate and prepares the deed.

With no lender, the closing date rests on the title work and your preference. Military families with orders, owners of inherited homes and landlords with a vacant unit are some of the people who ask about this route. We do not promise a price before seeing the property.

More questions about Fountain, CO

Is Fountain in El Paso County?

Yes. Fountain is a home rule city in El Paso County, about 10 miles south of downtown Colorado Springs. Property taxes are billed by the El Paso County Treasurer and deeds are recorded with the county clerk and recorder.

Which school district is my Fountain house in?

Most of Fountain is in Fountain School District 8, the north is in Widefield District 3, and small parts fall into Hanover District 28 and Harrison District 2. Confirm your address with the district.

Who provides electricity and water in Fountain?

City of Fountain Utilities provides both. It was established in 1919 and serves about 48,000 people in and around Fountain. Call (719) 322-2010 to schedule a final reading when you sell.

How do I find out my property tax balance before closing?

Ask the El Paso County Treasurer for a payoff figure at (719) 520-7900, and have your title company order a Certificate of Taxes Due. Unpaid prior-year balances can end up in the tax lien sale.

Can I sell my Fountain house if it needs repairs?

Yes. A cash buyer purchases as-is, so you do not have to complete repairs first. The offer accounts for the condition of the house.
